description: A status's attendance is the number of different members who attended any event with that status.

b.request: Count distinct members who attended any event with each event status (joining attendance to event on event_id, excluding attendance rows with no matching event), then report each status's distinct attendee count and its share of the total distinct-attendee count summed across all statuses, unrounded
b.sql: WITH status_counts AS (SELECT e.status, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attendee_count FROM attendance a INNER JOIN event e ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.status), total AS (SELECT SUM(attendee_count) AS total_count FROM status_counts) SELECT s.status, s.attendee_count, CAST(s.attendee_count AS REAL) / NULLIF(t.total_count, 0) AS share FROM status_counts s CROSS JOIN total t;

c.request: Taking attendance entries that match an event (others left out), how many attendees does each event `status` have, and what share of the total across all statuses is that? Show the status, its number of attendees, and the share, without rounding. A status's attendance is the number of different members who attended any event with that status.
c.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attendees, CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member)) OVER () AS share FROM attendance AS a JOIN event AS e ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.status;

a.request: Match attendance entries to their events (drop entries with no matching event). For each event `status`, show the status, the number of different members who attended at least one event with that status (a member who attended three such events adds one), and that number divided by the sum of these per-status numbers over all statuses. Do not round.
a.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS member_count, CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member)) OVER () AS member_ratio FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.status;

d.request: Taking attendance entries that match an event (others left out), how many different members attended any event with each event `status`, and what share of the total across all statuses is that? Show the status, its number of distinct attendees, and the share, without rounding.
d.sql: WITH status_attendees AS (SELECT e.status AS status, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attendees FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event GROUP BY e.status) SELECT status, attendees, CAST(attendees AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(attendees) FROM status_attendees) AS share FROM status_attendees;
